security_audit.summary: Most external command detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline examples, not executable skill code. The content still contains high-risk dual-use API exploitation guidance, including local file access payloads, SSRF and internal port probes, sensitive data extraction examples, IP disclosure, and rate-limit evasion guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Replace file:///etc/passwd examples with benign mock paths and frame checks as detection-only tests for authorized targets.
Remove localhost port probing, SMB or DNS attacker callbacks, and iplogger examples, or replace them with private lab endpoints.
Add written scope prerequisites, consent checks, safe lab guidance, and refusal guidance for live targets without permission.
Remove IP rotation as a workaround and describe rate-limit testing through approved limits and coordinated test windows.

content.user_title: Test APIs for Bug Bounty Findings
content.value_statement: API testers need repeatable checks for hidden endpoints, authorization flaws, and injection issues. This skill organizes API fuzzing workflows for authorized bug bounty and penetration testing.
actual_capabilities: Outlines REST, SOAP, and GraphQL API test workflows.
Lists endpoint discovery and documentation review techniques.
Provides IDOR, method tampering, and content type test ideas.
Covers GraphQL introspection, batching, nested query, and injection checks.
Suggests tool categories and wordlists for API security assessment.
Includes troubleshooting tips for API responses and access controls.
limitations: Does not verify authorization or legal scope for a target.
Contains dual-use payloads that must only be used in approved environments.
Does not run tools or validate results by itself.
Requires tester judgment to avoid harmful traffic or service disruption.

use_cases.title: Plan a Bug Bounty API Review
use_cases.description: Create a scoped checklist for endpoint discovery, authorization checks, and evidence collection.

use_cases.title: Build an Internal API Test Checklist
use_cases.description: Translate API security topics into repeatable checks for product security reviews.

use_cases.title: Prepare GraphQL Assessment Tasks
use_cases.description: Organize GraphQL introspection, batching, nested query, and authorization tests for a client engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Start API Recon
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for an approved target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized API reconnaissance checklist for this scoped target. Include documentation review, endpoint discovery, version checks, and safe evidence notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review IDOR Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these scoped endpoints and role descriptions, suggest safe IDOR tests that avoid accessing real user data.

prompt_templates.title: Assess GraphQL Surface
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this GraphQL schema excerpt for risky queries, mutations, batching issues, and introspection exposure within a test environment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Full API Fuzzing
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a phased fuzzing plan for my approved bug bounty target, including scope controls, rate limits, evidence collection, and reporting criteria.

output_examples.input: Help me test an in-scope API for IDOR.
output_examples.output: A prioritized checklist covering object identifiers, role pairs, negative controls, and evidence notes for authorized testing.

output_examples.input: Review a GraphQL endpoint for common risks.
output: Check whether introspection is exposed in production.
Review mutations for missing authorization checks.
Test batching and nested queries within approved limits.

output_examples.input: Turn my API findings into a report outline.
output_examples.output: A report structure with summary, affected endpoints, impact, reproduction steps, evidence, and remediation guidance.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before testing any endpoint.
Use synthetic accounts and test data when checking authorization boundaries.
Throttle requests and coordinate risky tests with the program owner.
anti_patterns: Testing production APIs without permission or outside listed scope.
Using payloads that exfiltrate real files, secrets, or personal data.
Bypassing rate limits with IP rotation instead of approved test windows.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only on APIs where you have written permission and a defined scope.

faq.question: Can it run API fuzzing tools?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflows and prompts. You must choose tools and operate them responsibly.

faq.question: Does it support GraphQL testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers introspection, batching, nested queries, and GraphQL authorization review.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes, but beginners should start in a lab or approved training target.

faq.question: What evidence should I collect?
faq.answer: Collect endpoint details, request context, account roles, screenshots, timestamps, and clear impact notes.

faq.question: How should risky tests be handled?
faq.answer: Coordinate with the owner, use test data, limit request volume, and stop if impact exceeds scope.
